pass_io.py:113-120 builds the record with `timestamp_ns` as the 5th key; `{"timestamp_ns": ..., **record}` merges the caller's value but leaves the key at the leading position, shifting JSON key order in the serialized line
Functionally harmless: alert_store.is_deduped/patch_bug_filed access records by key (`rec.get(...)`), never by position
findings.finding: The plan's 'byte-for-byte unchanged / no existing stamper changes' claim for central stamping is inaccurate: with `{"timestamp_ns": time.time_ns(), **record}`, existing callers whose record already contains `timestamp_ns` will have that key re-positioned to the FRONT of the dict (Python keeps a re-assigned key at its first insertion index), so json.dumps emits different key ordering and the JSONL bytes differ from today's output.
findings.location: Fix plan (AC#1 owner decision) — 'the dozen existing stampers are byte-for-byte unchanged' / Blast radius 'no existing stamper changes'
scenarios: Any of the 13 existing stampers (pass_io, fetcher, apply_handlers, etc.) whose emitted JSONL line is compared byte-for-byte in a snapshot/golden test
A reviewer trusting the 'byte-identical' claim and skipping verification of existing-stamper output
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the rationale as 'value-preserving (caller value wins), not byte-preserving' and note that existing stampers' JSONL key ORDER shifts (timestamp_ns moves to front) but semantics are unchanged; alternatively, to keep existing output identical, place the default only when absent: `record = {**record} if 'timestamp_ns' in record else {**record, 'timestamp_ns': time.time_ns()}` (or `record.setdefault('timestamp_ns', time.time_ns())` on a copy).
